## 2

I understand why some images can seem suspicious—photos can be edited, and institutions can make mistakes. But the evidence for a spherical Earth doesn’t depend on space photos. We can observe ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, different stars from different latitudes, Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, time zones, and satellite communication. These are independent observations that fit a round Earth consistently; they would be very difficult to explain with a flat one.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it contains many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than red light, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky. That is why the sky usually looks blue. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere; much of the blue gets scattered away, leaving more red and orange light.
